key_insight: A hybrid wave-mode formulation reduces wave-dispersion computation in 2D periodic structures by combining unit-cell modal reduction with a reduced wave-propagation basis.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports efficient vibration analysis of structurally realistic periodic panels using standard finite-element models.
method: Use component mode synthesis to represent unit-cell dynamics and local resonances.
Project the wave-propagation spectral problem onto a reduced set of propagating-wave shape functions.
Combine both reductions within a wave finite element framework.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an application to a bidirectionally stiffened panel, examining reduction parameters and numerical robustness, but provides no quantitative error or speedup figures.
watch_item: Reduced-basis selection requires care to preserve relevant local resonances and propagating waves.
paper_title: A hybrid wave-mode formulation for the vibro-acoustic analysis of 2D periodic structures
